questions.q: When does WHILE check its condition?
options: Before each pass through the loop
Only once, before the loop starts
After each pass, never before
WHILE does not check a condition at all
questions.explain: WHILE keeps running the block as long as the condition evaluates to TRUE at the start of each pass.

questions.q: What happens if nothing inside a WHILE loop ever makes the condition false?
options: The loop runs forever (an infinite loop)
SQL Server automatically stops it after 100 iterations
It throws a compile-time error before running
It runs exactly once and then stops
questions.explain: This is why incrementing a counter (or otherwise changing the condition) inside the loop is essential.

questions.q: What does BREAK do inside a WHILE loop?
options: Exits the loop immediately, regardless of the WHILE condition
Skips only the current iteration and continues looping
Pauses the loop until manually resumed
Restarts the loop from the beginning
questions.explain: BREAK stops the loop outright, even if the WHILE condition would otherwise still be true.

questions.q: What does CONTINUE do differently from BREAK?
options: It skips the rest of the current pass and jumps back to re-checking the WHILE condition, without exiting the loop
It exits the loop entirely, same as BREAK
It permanently disables the loop's condition check
It has no functional difference from BREAK
questions.explain: CONTINUE keeps the loop running, just skipping ahead to the next iteration's check.

questions.q: Why do experienced T-SQL developers use WHILE loops less often than in other programming languages?
options: T-SQL is fundamentally set-based, and operating on entire tables at once is usually faster than looping row-by-row
WHILE loops are deprecated in modern SQL Server
WHILE cannot be combined with IF/ELSE
WHILE loops can only run a maximum of 10 times
questions.explain: Reaching for a set-based query (JOIN, UPDATE, CASE) instead of WHILE is often the better, faster approach in T-SQL.
